answer: Each identity must operate one uniquely registered weather mast for 30 days and lock 2,700 units against spoofing. After every dawn it posts a signed telemetry strip to a public knoll archive. Two masts that share a radio fingerprint, power signature, or funding source lose the bond. An honest operator spends 2,700 units and tends one mast. To field 140 aliases, an attacker must deploy 140 distinct masts and lock 378,000 units; a compact falcon radio moved between sites is rejected when its spectrum fingerprint or clock drift repeats.
